previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient, a woman with poorly controlled type II diabetes and a history of diabetic retinopathy, was admitted with shortness of breath and a productive cough. She was found to have multifocal pneumonia on chest X-ray, involving the left lower and right upper lobes, and was treated with intravenous then oral levofloxacin. She also presented with metabolic acidosis and hyperglycemia, which improved with IV fluids and insulin therapy. Metformin was held during admission due to acidosis risk but was restarted before discharge. Her condition stabilized, and she was discharged home on a continued insulin regimen, metformin, lisinopril, and a three-day course of oral levofloxacin. Follow-up was advised for a repeat chest X-ray in six weeks and primary care evaluation of her diabetes control.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ yo F with DM2, HTN, depression, and recent noncompliance with 
insulin ___ confusion about dosage who presented to ___ office 
with hyperglycemia sent to ___ for treatment.

While ___ house, the patient was first admitted to the ICU 
setting after an insulin gtt and SQ insulin was administered 
with IVF ___ the emergency room.  ___ AG was 16 at time of 
presentation, and soon after admission to the ICU, ___ gap 
closed and ___ phosphate was agressively repleted.  She was 
started on an ISS and ___ home metformin was held while ___ 
house.  She was called out to the medical floor where a thorough 
physical exam revealed a collection of large abscesses along the 
medial thigh.  The patient notably became febrile on HD2-3.  
Surgery was c/s'ed and they performed an I/D on the abscess.  We 
started the patient empirically on broad spectrum abx and she 
was ultimately discharged on augmentin for a 10 day course with 
close PCP follow ___.  ___ insulin continued to be titrated and 
she was also set up to see the nutritionist for ___ diabetes 
education.  At time of discharge, ___ insulin was increased and 
___ metformin was discontinued. 

HOSPITAL COURSE BY PROBLEM
# Hyperglycemia/diabetes: Pt has been noncompliant with insulin 
as the most likely cause of hyperglycemia.  She states she 
stopped using it for 6 days PTA given that she was confused by 
the dosage.  We were also concerned about an infectious etiology 
given low grade fevers, and she did spike a fever on HD 3.  A 
thorough exam revealed a large abscess ___ the medial thighs 
bilaterally (3 separate abscesses).  Please see below for 
further details regarding management of this abscess.  Notably, 
a UA, CXR, and blood Cxs were all negative.  As above, ___ terms 
of the management of ___ DKA/HHS, she did receive ~ 10 L of NS 
given ___ severe dehydration and tachycardia throughout ___ 
hospital course.  She was briefly on an insulin gtt ___ the ED 
with SQ humalog as well, and ___ presenting AG was 16.  This gap 
closed while she was ___ the ICU, and she was able to tolerate a 
full meal ___ the ICU prior to transfer to the medical floor.  
___ home regimen was restarted while ___ the ICU, and we titrated 
this up to 28 units of humalog mix ___ the AM and 30 units at 
dinner time by the time of discharge.  ___ sugars were under 
better control at that time with a fasting sugar at dinner time 
of 173, HS of 92, and breakfast of 137.  We discontinued ___ 
metformin at time of discharge, and ensured she had insulin 
teaching as well as a visit with a nutritionist regarding 
diabetes diet education (as she was noted to eat ___ and 
other fast food meals provided by family while ___ house).  
Throughout ___ course, no abdominal pain, or other common si/sx 
of DKA.  No confusion or AMS.  

# Abscess:  Surgery was consulted and I/D was performed with 
cultures growing polymicrobial collections as expected 
(specifically heavy growth of Group B Strep, sparse of coag + 
staph as well as corynebacterium).  She was empirically started 
on broad abx (vanc/cipro/flagyl) for a period of 2 days and 
transitioned to PO Augmentin for 24 hours ___ house for 
monitoring.  As she did not have any more fevers and she did not 
develop a leukocytosis (she indeed did not develop one at all 
during ___ course), she was discharged with only Augmentin to 
finish a total of a 10 day antibiotic course.  Of note, this 
does not cover MRSA, and luckily ___ cx speciated to MSSA by 
time of discharge.  For follow up, ___ cultures will need to be 
followed ___ the outpatient arena.
  
# Anemia: Hct 32 from 37, ___ the setting of receiving 5L of NS 
___ ED and MICU. Pt has no si/sxs of LH or dizziness. Baseline 
Hct seems to be anywhere between 32 and 36.  ___ Hct continued 
to trend down to 29.  A thorough work up was done which showed 
B12 was normal, and she had iron indicies that seemed to 
indicate both iron deficiency anemia as well as anemia of 
chronic disease (low iron, normal ferritin, low 
TIBC/Transferrin).  Initiation of iron therapy will be deferred 
to the outpatient arena given that we would like to prioritize 
___ taking abx after discharge.
  
# Tachycardia: Anemia is not profound enough to account for 
tachycardia, and seems to be sinus tachycardia. Most likely 
thought was that this was ___ dehydration ___ the setting of 
osmotic diuresis with DKA/HHS.  She was aggressively bolused and 
as above received ~ 10 L of NS ___ house.  We were also concerned 
about possible thyroid issues given possible proptosis on exam, 
however TSH was wnl (Free T4 was slightly low, c/w sick 
euthyroid).  ___ tachycardia resolved with fluid resuscitation 
and with fever management.  OF note, ___ BP was stable 
throughout all of this given concern for evolving sepsis ___ 
someone with a large abscess, but as above, clinically she 
remained well without other HD signs of instability.
  
# HTN: Pt is on lisinopril, currently still receiving 
medication.  We continued the home dose.  
  
# depression - pt denies SI as being an active reason for 
missing insulin doses.  There was slight concern for this being 
the reason for poor compliance, however given denial, no further 
w/u was pursued.  She was continued on paxil.
  
# Diarrhea: Pt did not receive abx prior to ___ diarrhea.  A 
C-diff was sent and was negative.  This resolved over time.

# FOLLOW UP ISSUES:
- Patient had multiple cultures to be followed up (wound, blood 
cultures)
- Patient will require close f/u with PCP regarding diabetes 
education/management.  SHe did see a diabetic counselor ___ terms 
of diet while ___ house.
- We discontinued metformin.  If this is to be restarted, would 
consider changing insulin dosing.
- Abscess will need to be monitored to ensure adequate healing. 
Pt will have f/u ___ ACS/Surgery clinic ___ 2 weeks time, as well 
as ___ to help with dressing changes.
